verses.1:1: In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, so that the word of the Lord from the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the Lord roused the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he sent out a proclamation throughout his entire kingdom, also in writing, saying:
verses.1:2: "This is what Cyrus king of the Persians says: The Lord God of heaven has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He Himself has commanded me to build a house for Him in Jerusalem, which is in Judea.
verses.1:3: Who among you is of His entire people? May his God be with him. Let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judea, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel; He Himself is the God who is in Jerusalem.
verses.1:4: And all the rest, in every place wherever they dwell, let the men from his place assist him with silver and gold, with possessions, and with livestock, besides what they voluntarily offer to the temple of God, which is in Jerusalem."
verses.1:5: And the leaders of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, and everyone whose spirit God had roused, arose so that they might go up to build the temple of the Lord, which was in Jerusalem.
verses.1:6: And all those who were on every side assisted their hands with silver and gold vessels, with possessions and beasts of burden, with furnishings, besides those things which they had offered of their own accord.
verses.1:7: King Cyrus also brought out the vessels of the temple of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, and he had placed them in the temple of his god.
verses.1:8: Now Cyrus king of the Persians brought them out by the hand of Mithredath the son of Gazabar and counted them out to Sheshbazzar, the leader of Judah.
verses.1:9: And this is their number: thirty gold basins, one thousand silver basins, twenty-nine knives, thirty gold goblets,
verses.1:10: four hundred ten silver goblets of a second type, one thousand other vessels.
verses.1:11: All the gold and silver vessels were five thousand four hundred; Sheshbazzar brought all of them with those who were going up from the exile of Babylon to Jerusalem.
verses.2:1: Now these are the sons of the province who went up from the captivity that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had deported to Babylon, and they returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each one to his own city.
verses.2:2: They came with Zerubbabel, Joshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
verses.2:3: The sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
verses.2:4: The sons of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy-two.
verses.2:5: The sons of Arah, seven hundred seventy-five.
verses.2:6: The sons of Pahath-moab, of the sons of Joshua: Joab, two thousand eight hundred twelve.
verses.2:7: The sons of Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
verses.2:8: The sons of Zattu, nine hundred forty-five.
verses.2:9: The sons of Zaccai, seven hundred sixty.
verses.2:10: The sons of Bani, six hundred forty-two.
verses.2:11: The sons of Bebai, six hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:12: The sons of Azgad, one thousand two hundred twenty-two.
verses.2:13: The sons of Adonikam, six hundred sixty-six.
verses.2:14: The sons of Bigvai, two thousand fifty-six.
verses.2:15: The sons of Adin, four hundred fifty-four.
verses.2:16: The sons of Ater, who were from Hezekiah, ninety-eight.
verses.2:17: The sons of Bezai, three hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:18: The sons of Jorah, one hundred twelve.
verses.2:19: The sons of Hashum, two hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:21: The sons of Bethlehem, one hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:23: The men of Anathoth, one hundred twenty-eight.
verses.2:25: The sons of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred forty-three.
verses.2:26: The sons of Ramah and Geba, six hundred twenty-one.
verses.2:27: The men of Michmas, one hundred twenty-two.
verses.2:28: The men of Bethel and Ai, two hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:30: The sons of Magbish, one hundred fifty-six.
verses.2:31: The sons of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
verses.2:32: The sons of Harim, three hundred twenty.
verses.2:33: The sons of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred twenty-five.
verses.2:34: The sons of Jericho, three hundred forty-five.
verses.2:35: The sons of Senaah, three thousand six hundred thirty.
verses.2:36: The priests: the sons of Jedaiah in the house of Joshua, nine hundred seventy-three.
verses.2:37: The sons of Immer, one thousand fifty-two.
verses.2:38: The sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred forty-seven.
verses.2:39: The sons of Harim, one thousand seventeen.
verses.2:40: The Levites: the sons of Joshua and Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodaviah, seventy-four.
verses.2:41: The singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred twenty-eight.
verses.2:42: The sons of the gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Shobai; in all, one hundred thirty-nine.
verses.2:43: The Nethinim: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,
verses.2:44: the sons of Keros, the sons of Siaha, the sons of Padon,
verses.2:45: the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Akkub,
verses.2:46: the sons of Hagab, the sons of Shamlai, the sons of Hanan,
verses.2:47: the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar, the sons of Reaiah,
verses.2:48: the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda, the sons of Gazzam,
verses.2:49: the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah, the sons of Besai,
verses.2:50: the sons of Asnah, the sons of Meunim, the sons of Nephusim,
verses.2:51: the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,
verses.2:52: the sons of Bazluth, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha,
verses.2:53: the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah,
verses.2:54: the sons of Neziah, the sons of Hatipha;
verses.2:55: the sons of the servants of Solomon: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Peruda,
verses.2:56: the sons of Jaalah, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,
verses.2:57: the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth, who were from Hazzebaim, the sons of Ami:
verses.2:58: all the Nethinim and the sons of the servants of Solomon, three hundred ninety-two.
verses.2:59: And these are the ones who went up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer; and they could not declare the house of their fathers and their lineage, whether they were from Israel.
verses.2:60: The sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda, six hundred fifty-two.
verses.2:61: And of the sons of the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, the sons of Barzillai, who took a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
verses.2:62: These searched for the written record of their genealogy and did not find it, and they were expelled from the priesthood.
verses.2:63: And the Tirshatha told them not to eat from the Holy of Holies until a learned and perfect priest should arise.
verses.2:64: The whole multitude, as one, was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,
verses.2:65: excluding their male servants and female servants, who were seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven; and among them were two hundred male and female singers.
verses.2:66: Their horses were seven hundred thirty-six; their mules, two hundred forty-five;
verses.2:67: their camels, four hundred thirty-five; their donkeys, six thousand seven hundred twenty.
verses.2:68: And some of the leaders of the fathers, when they entered the temple of the Lord, which is in Jerusalem, voluntarily offered for the house of God to build it up in its place.
verses.2:69: According to their means, they gave the expenses of the work: sixty-one thousand solidi of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priestly garments.
verses.2:70: So the priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the Nethinim settled in their towns, and all Israel in their cities.
verses.3:1: And now the seventh month had come, and the sons of Israel were in their cities; therefore the people were gathered together as one man in Jerusalem.
verses.3:2: And Joshua son of Jozadak, and his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and his brothers, arose and built the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
verses.3:3: Now they set the altar of God on its bases, while the peoples of the lands all around were terrifying them; and they offered on it a burnt offering to the Lord morning and evening.
verses.3:4: And they kept the Feast of Tabernacles, as it is written, and offered the burnt offering day by day in order, according to the ordinance, the work of each day on its own day.
verses.3:5: And after these things, the continual burnt offering, both at the new moons and at all the feasts of the Lord that were consecrated, and on all occasions in which a gift was freely offered to the Lord.
verses.3:6: From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer a burnt offering to the Lord; however, the foundation of the temple of God had not yet been laid.
verses.3:7: Now they gave money to the stonecutters and masons, and also food, drink, and oil to the Sidonians and Tyrians, so that they would bring cedar timbers from Lebanon to the sea of Joppa, according to what Cyrus, king of the Persians, had commanded them.
verses.3:8: Now in the second year of their coming to the temple of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Joshua son of Jozadak, and the rest of their brothers, the priests and the Levites, and all who had come from the captivity to Jerusalem, began, and they appointed the Levites from twenty years old and upward to press forward the work of the Lord.
verses.3:9: And Joshua and his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, and the sons of Judah stood as one man to urge on those who were doing the work in the temple of God: the sons of Henadad, and their sons, and their brothers the Levites.
verses.3:10: Therefore, when the foundation of the temple of the Lord had been laid by the masons, the priests stood in their vestments with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise God by the hands of David, king of Israel.
verses.3:11: And they sang together in hymns and thanksgiving to the Lord: "For He is good, for His mercy is forever over Israel." All the people also shouted with a loud shout in praising the Lord, because the foundation of the temple of the Lord had been laid.
verses.3:12: Very many also of the priests and Levites, and the chiefs of the fathers, and the elders, who had seen the former temple when it was founded, and this temple before their eyes, wept with a loud voice; and many, shouting in joy, lifted up their voice.
verses.3:13: Nor could anyone distinguish the sound of the shout of those rejoicing and the sound of the weeping of the people; for the people shouted mingled together with a loud shout, and the sound was heard far away.
verses.4:1: Now the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the sons of the captivity were building a temple to the Lord God of Israel.
verses.4:2: And approaching Zerubbabel and the chiefs of the fathers, they said to them, "Let us build with you, for just like you, we seek your God; look, we have offered sacrifices since the days of Esarhaddon, king of Assyria, who brought us here."
verses.4:3: And Zerubbabel, and Joshua, and the rest of the chiefs of the fathers of Israel said to them, "It is not for you and us to build a house to our God, but we ourselves alone will build to the Lord our God, as Cyrus, king of the Persians, commanded us."
verses.4:4: So it happened that the people of the land hindered the hands of the people of Judah and troubled them in building.
verses.4:5: Moreover, they hired counselors against them to overthrow their counsel all the days of Cyrus, king of the Persians, and until the reign of Darius, king of the Persians.
verses.4:6: And in the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.4:7: And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, and Tabeel, and the rest who were in their council, wrote to Artaxerxes, king of the Persians; and the letter of accusation was written in Syriac and was read in the Syrian language.
verses.4:8: Rehum Beelteem and Shimshai the scribe wrote one letter concerning Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes, of this sort:
verses.4:9: Rehum Beelteem, and Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their counselors, the Dinaites, and the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians, the Susanchites, the Dehavites, and the Elamites,
verses.4:10: and the rest of the nations whom the great and glorious Osnappar deported and made to dwell in the cities of Samaria and in the remaining regions beyond the river in peace
verses.4:11: (this is the copy of the letter that they sent to him): "To King Artaxerxes, your servants, the men who are beyond the river, send greetings.
verses.4:12: Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from you to us have come to Jerusalem, the rebellious and most wicked city, which they are building, erecting its walls and repairing the house walls.
verses.4:13: Now therefore let it be known to the king that if that city is built and its walls are restored, they will not pay tribute, toll, or yearly revenues, and this harm will reach even to the kings.
verses.4:14: Now we, mindful of the salt that we have eaten in the palace, and because we consider it wrong to see injuries to the king, have therefore sent and informed the king,
verses.4:15: so that you may search in the books of the histories of your fathers, and you will find it written in the records, and you will know that that city is a rebellious city, and harmful to kings and provinces, and wars have been stirred up in it from ancient days; for which reason the city itself was also destroyed.
verses.4:16: We inform the king that if that city is built and its walls are restored, you will have no possession beyond the river."
verses.4:17: The king sent word to Rehum Beelteem, and Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest who were in their council, inhabitants of Samaria, and to the others beyond the river, sending greetings and peace:
verses.4:18: "The accusation that you sent to us has been clearly read before me,
verses.4:19: and a command was given by me, and they searched and found that that city from ancient days has rebelled against kings, and that seditions and battles have been stirred up in it;
verses.4:20: for very mighty kings have also been in Jerusalem, who also ruled over the entire region that is beyond the river; they also received tribute, toll, and revenues.
verses.4:21: Now therefore hear the decree: stop those men, so that that city may not be built until perhaps an order is given by me.
verses.4:22: See to it that you do not carry this out negligently, and that evil does not gradually grow against the kings."
verses.4:23: Therefore the copy of the edict of King Artaxerxes was read before Rehum Beelteem, and Shimshai the scribe, and their counselors; and they went in haste to Jerusalem to the Jews, and stopped them by arm and strength.
verses.4:24: Then the work of the house of the Lord in Jerusalem was suspended, and it was not done until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of the Persians.
verses.5:1: Now Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied, prophesying to the Jews who were in Judea and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel.
verses.5:2: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Joshua son of Jozadak arose and began to build the temple of God in Jerusalem, and with them were the prophets of God, helping them.
verses.5:3: At that very time Tattenai, who was governor beyond the river, and Shethar-bozenai, and their counselors came to them, and they said to them in this way: "Who gave you counsel to build this house and to restore its walls?"
verses.5:4: To this we answered them what the names were of the men who were the originators of that building.
verses.5:5: But the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews, and they could not stop them. And it seemed good that the matter should be referred to Darius, and then they would give satisfaction against that accusation.
verses.5:6: The copy of the letter that Tattenai, governor of the region beyond the river, and Shethar-bozenai, and his counselors, the Apharsachites, who were beyond the river, sent to King Darius.
verses.5:7: The message that they had sent to him was written as follows: "To King Darius, all peace.
verses.5:8: Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judea, to the house of the great God, which is being built with unpolished stone, and timbers are being laid in the walls; and that work is being diligently constructed and is growing in their hands.
verses.5:9: Therefore we questioned those elders, and we spoke to them in this way: 'Who gave you authority to build this house and to restore these walls?'
verses.5:10: Moreover, we asked them for their names so that we might inform you, and we wrote down the names of those men who are leaders among them.
verses.5:11: And they answered us with a reply of this sort, saying, 'We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are building the temple that had been constructed many years ago, and which a great king of Israel had built and constructed.
verses.5:12: But after our fathers provoked the God of heaven to anger, He delivered them into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, the Chaldean; he also destroyed this house and deported its people to Babylon.
verses.5:13: However, in the first year of Cyrus, king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued an edict that this house of God should be built.
verses.5:14: For the gold and silver vessels of the temple of God also, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple that was in Jerusalem and had carried away into the temple of Babylon, King Cyrus brought out from the temple of Babylon, and they were given to one named Sheshbazzar, whom he also appointed ruler,
verses.5:15: and he said to him, "Take these vessels, and go, and place them in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be built in its place."
verses.5:16: So then that Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the temple of God in Jerusalem, and from that time until now it is being built, and it has not yet been completed.'
verses.5:17: Now therefore, if it seems good to the king, let him search in the library of the king, which is in Babylon, whether an order was given by King Cyrus that the house of God in Jerusalem should be built, and let him send to us the will of the king concerning this matter."
verses.6:1: Then King Darius gave a command, and they searched in the library of books that were stored in Babylon.
verses.6:2: And in Ecbatana, which is a fortress in the province of Media, one scroll was found, and such a record was written in it:
verses.6:3: "In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus decreed that the house of God, which is in Jerusalem, be built in the place where they offer sacrifices, and that they lay foundations supporting a height of sixty cubits and a width of sixty cubits,
verses.6:4: three courses of unpolished stones, and likewise courses of new timber; and the expenses will be given from the house of the king.
verses.6:5: Moreover, let the gold and silver vessels of the temple of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple of Jerusalem and brought into Babylon, be restored and carried back into the temple in Jerusalem to their own place, which were also placed in the temple of God."
verses.6:6: "Now therefore, Tattenai, governor of the region that is beyond the river, Shethar-bozenai, and your counselors the Apharsachites, who are beyond the river, stay far away from them,
verses.6:7: and allow that temple of God to be made by the governor of the Jews and by their elders, so that they may build that house of God in its own place.
verses.6:8: Moreover, it has been commanded by me what ought to be done by those elders of the Jews so that the house of God may be built: namely, that from the king's coffer, that is, from the tributes that are given from the region beyond the river, expenses be carefully given to those men, so that the work may not be hindered.
verses.6:9: And if it is necessary, calves, and lambs, and young goats for a burnt offering to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the rite of the priests who are in Jerusalem, let it be given to them day by day, so that there may be no complaint in anything.
verses.6:10: And let them offer offerings to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king and of his sons.
verses.6:11: Therefore a decree has been laid down by me: as for every man who alters this order, let a beam be taken from his own house and set upright, and let him be impaled on it, and let his house be confiscated.
verses.6:12: And may God, who caused His name to dwell there, destroy all kingdoms and the people that stretches out its hand to resist and destroy that house of God which is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have established a decree, which I wish to be carefully fulfilled."
verses.6:13: Therefore Tattenai, governor of the region beyond the river, and Shethar-bozenai, and his counselors thus diligently carried it out, according to what King Darius had commanded.
verses.6:14: And the elders of the Jews were building and prospering according to the prophecy of Haggai the prophet and of Zechariah the son of Iddo; and they built and constructed by the command of the God of Israel, and by the command of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes, kings of the Persians,
verses.6:15: and they completed this house of God by the third day of the month of Adar, which is the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
verses.6:16: And the sons of Israel, the priests and the Levites, and the rest of the sons of the exile celebrated the dedication of the house of God with joy.
verses.6:17: And they offered for the dedication of the house of God one hundred calves, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and twelve male goats for the sin of all Israel, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
verses.6:18: And they appointed the priests in their divisions, and the Levites in their courses, over the works of God in Jerusalem, just as it is written in the book of Moses.
verses.6:19: And the sons of Israel of the exile celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.6:20: For the priests and the Levites had been purified as one, all of them clean to sacrifice the Passover for all the sons of the exile, and for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.
verses.6:21: And the sons of Israel who had returned from the exile ate, and all who had separated themselves to them from the defilement of the nations of the land, to seek the Lord God of Israel.
verses.6:22: And they celebrated the festival of unleavened bread for seven days with gladness, because the Lord had made them glad and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, to help their hands in the work of the house of the Lord God of Israel.
verses.7:1: Now after these matters, in the reign of Artaxerxes, king of the Persians, Ezra the son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,
verses.7:2: the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,
verses.7:3: the son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,
verses.7:4: the son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,
verses.7:5: the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, the priest from the beginning.
verses.7:6: This Ezra went up from Babylon, and he was a swift scribe in the law of Moses, which the Lord God gave to Israel; and the king gave him all his request, according to the hand of the Lord his God upon him.
verses.7:7: And some of the sons of Israel, and of the sons of the priests, and of the sons of the Levites, and of the singers, and of the gatekeepers, and of the Nethinim went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
verses.7:8: And they came to Jerusalem in the fifth month; that is the seventh year of the king.
verses.7:9: For on the first day of the first month he began to go up from Babylon, and on the first day of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God upon him.
verses.7:10: For Ezra prepared his heart to investigate the law of the Lord, and to do and to teach precept and judgment in Israel.
verses.7:11: Now this is the copy of the letter of the edict which King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, a scribe instructed in the words and precepts of the Lord, and in His ceremonies in Israel:
verses.7:12: "Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, most learned scribe of the law of the God of heaven, greetings.
verses.7:13: It has been decreed by me that whoever in my kingdom, of the people of Israel, and of its priests, and of the Levites, chooses to go to Jerusalem may go with you.
verses.7:14: For from the presence of the king and of his seven counselors you have been sent to inspect Judea and Jerusalem in the law of your God, which is in your hand,
verses.7:15: and to carry the silver and gold which the king and his counselors have voluntarily offered to the God of Israel, whose tabernacle is in Jerusalem.
verses.7:16: And all the silver and gold, whatever you find in the entire province of Babylon and the people wish to offer, and from the priests the things they voluntarily offer for the house of their God, which is in Jerusalem,
verses.7:17: freely receive, and carefully buy with this money calves, rams, lambs, and sacrifices and their drink offerings, and offer them upon the altar of the temple of your God, which is in Jerusalem.
verses.7:18: Moreover, if it pleases you and your brothers to do anything with the remaining silver and gold, do it according to the will of your God.
verses.7:19: The vessels also, which are given to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver in the sight of God in Jerusalem.
verses.7:20: Moreover, the other things that are needed for the house of your God, however much it is necessary for you to spend, will be given from the treasury and from the king's exchequer,
verses.7:21: and from me. I, King Artaxerxes, have established and decreed to all the keepers of the public coffer who are beyond the river, that whatever Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of heaven, requests from you, you give without delay,
verses.7:22: up to one hundred talents of silver, and up to one hundred kors of wheat, and up to one hundred baths of wine, and up to one hundred baths of oil, and salt without measure.
verses.7:23: Everything that pertains to the rite of the God of heaven, let it be diligently provided in the house of the God of heaven, so that He may not perhaps become angry against the kingdom of the king and of his sons.
verses.7:24: We also make known to you concerning all the priests, and the Levites, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, the Nethinim, and the servants of this house of God, that you have no authority to impose tax, tribute, or annual dues upon them.
verses.7:25: And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God, which is in your hand, appoint judges and magistrates, so that they may judge all the people who are beyond the river, namely, those who know the law of your God; and also freely teach the uninstructed.
verses.7:26: And as for everyone who does not diligently do the law of your God and the law of the king, judgment will be upon him, whether to death, or to banishment, or to the condemnation of his property, or indeed to prison."
verses.7:27: Blessed be the Lord God of our fathers, who put this in the heart of the king, to glorify the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem,
verses.7:28: and inclined His mercy toward me before the king and his counselors, and all the mighty leaders of the king; and I, strengthened by the hand of the Lord my God which was in me, gathered from Israel leaders to go up with me.
verses.8:1: These, therefore, are the leaders of the families, and the genealogy of those who went up with me from Babylon in the reign of King Artaxerxes.
verses.8:2: Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom. Of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel. Of the sons of David, Hattush.
verses.8:3: Of the sons of Shecaniah, the sons of Parosh, Zechariah; and with him one hundred fifty men were counted.
verses.8:4: Of the sons of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai the son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred men.
verses.8:5: Of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Ezekiel, and with him three hundred men.
verses.8:6: Of the sons of Adin, Ebed the son of Jonathan, and with him fifty men.
verses.8:7: Of the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah, and with him seventy men.
verses.8:8: Of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah the son of Michael, and with him eighty men.
verses.8:9: Of the sons of Joab, Obadiah the son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred eighteen men.
verses.8:10: Of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him one hundred sixty men.
verses.8:11: Of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah the son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men.
verses.8:12: Of the sons of Azgad, Johanan the son of Hakkatan, and with him one hundred ten men.
verses.8:13: Of the sons of Adonikam, who were the last; and these are their names: Eliphelet, and Jeiel, and Shemaiah, and with them sixty men.
verses.8:14: Of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with them seventy men.
verses.8:15: Now I gathered them at the river that flows to Ahava, and we remained there three days; and I searched among the people and among the priests for any of the sons of Levi, and I found none there.
verses.8:16: Therefore I sent Eliezer, and Ariel, and Shemaiah, and Elnathan, and Jarib, and another Elnathan, and Nathan, and Zechariah, and Meshullam, leaders; and Joiarib and Elnathan, wise men.
verses.8:17: And I sent them to Iddo, who is the chief in the place of Casiphia, and I put words in their mouth that they should speak to Iddo and his brothers, the Nethinim, in the place of Casiphia, so that they might bring to us ministers of the house of our God.
verses.8:18: And they brought to us, by the good hand of our God upon us, a most learned man of the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel, and Sherebiah, and his sons and his brothers, eighteen,
verses.8:19: and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, and his brothers and his sons, twenty;
verses.8:20: and of the Nethinim, whom David and the leaders had given for the services of the Levites, two hundred twenty Nethinim; all these were called by their own names.
verses.8:21: And I proclaimed a fast there beside the river Ahava, so that we might afflict ourselves before the Lord our God, and ask from Him a straight way for us and our children, and for all our possessions.
verses.8:22: For I was ashamed to ask the king for help and horsemen who would defend us from the enemy on the way, because we had said to the king, "The hand of our God is upon all who seek Him in goodness, and His dominion, and His strength, and wrath are upon all who abandon Him."
verses.8:23: So we fasted and petitioned our God for this, and it turned out favorably for us.
verses.8:24: And I separated twelve from the leaders of the priests: Sherebiah and Hashabiah, and with them ten of their brothers;
verses.8:25: and I weighed out to them the silver and the gold, and the consecrated vessels of the house of our God, which the king, and his counselors, and his leaders, and all Israel among those who had been found, had offered;
verses.8:26: and I weighed out into their hands six hundred fifty talents of silver, and one hundred silver vessels, one hundred talents of gold,
verses.8:27: and twenty golden bowls, which were worth a thousand solidi each, and two vessels of the finest gleaming bronze, as beautiful as gold.
verses.8:28: And I said to them, "You are holy to the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and gold that was freely offered to the Lord God of our fathers;
verses.8:29: watch and guard them until you weigh them out before the leaders of the priests and of the Levites, and the heads of the families of Israel in Jerusalem, into the treasury of the house of the Lord."
verses.8:30: So the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, to carry them to Jerusalem, into the house of our God.
verses.8:31: Therefore we set out from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month to go to Jerusalem; and the hand of our God was upon us, and He delivered us from the hand of the enemy and of the ambusher on the way.
verses.8:32: And we came to Jerusalem, and we remained there three days.
verses.8:33: Now on the fourth day, the silver, and the gold, and the vessels were weighed out in the house of our God by the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest, and with him was Eleazar the son of Phinehas, and with them were Jozabad the son of Joshua and Noadiah the son of Binnui, Levites,
verses.8:34: according to the number and weight of everything; and all the weight was written down at that time.
verses.8:35: Moreover, those who had come from captivity, the sons of the exile, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve young bulls for all the people of Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, twelve male goats for sin; all as a burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.8:36: And they delivered the king's edicts to the satraps who were from the king's presence, and to the governors beyond the river, and they lifted up the people and the house of God.
verses.9:1: Now after these things were completed, the leaders approached me, saying, "The people of Israel, the priests and the Levites, are not separated from the peoples of the lands and their abominations, namely, of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Jebusite, and of the Ammonites, and the Moabites, and the Egyptians, and the Amorites;
verses.9:2: for they have taken some of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, and they have mingled the holy seed with the peoples of the lands; indeed, the hand of the leaders and magistrates has been first in this transgression."
verses.9:3: And when I had heard this report, I tore my cloak and tunic, and pulled out hair from my head and beard, and sat down mourning.
verses.9:4: Then all who feared the word of the God of Israel gathered to me because of the transgression of those who had come from captivity, and I sat sorrowful until the evening sacrifice.
verses.9:5: And at the evening sacrifice, I rose up from my affliction, and with my cloak and tunic torn, I bowed my knees and spread out my hands to the Lord my God.
verses.9:6: And I said, "My God, I am ashamed and blush to lift up my face to You, because our iniquities have multiplied above our head, and our offenses have grown up to heaven,
verses.9:7: from the days of our fathers; and we ourselves also have sinned gravely up to this day, and in our iniquities we ourselves, and our kings, and our priests have been handed over into the hand of the kings of the lands, and to the sword, and to captivity, and to plunder, and to shame of face, as it is also on this day.
verses.9:8: And now, as it were for a little while and for a moment, our supplication has been made before the Lord our God, so that a remnant might be left to us, and a peg might be given to us in His holy place, and our God might enlighten our eyes, and give us a little life in our slavery;
verses.9:9: for we are slaves, and in our slavery our God has not abandoned us, but has inclined mercy upon us before the king of the Persians, to give us life, and to exalt the house of our God, and to rebuild its desolate places, and to give us a hedge in Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.9:10: And now, what shall we say, our God, after these things? For we have abandoned Your commandments,
verses.9:11: which You commanded by the hand of Your servants the prophets, saying, 'The land that you are entering so that you may possess it is an unclean land, according to the uncleanness of the peoples and of the other lands, with the abominations of those who have filled it from mouth to mouth in their defilement.
verses.9:12: Now therefore, do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take their daughters for your sons, and do not seek their peace and their prosperity forever, so that you may be strengthened, and eat the good things of the land, and have your sons as heirs for all ages.'
verses.9:13: And after all that has come upon us in our most evil deeds and in our great offense, since You, our God, have delivered us from our iniquity, and have given us salvation as it is today,
verses.9:14: so that we would not turn back and nullify Your commandments, nor join in marriage with the peoples of these abominations. Are You angry with us even to complete destruction, so that You would not leave us a remnant for salvation?
verses.9:15: Lord God of Israel, You are righteous, for we have been left to be saved, as on this day. Look, we are before You in our offense, for no one can stand before You because of this."
verses.10:1: So then, while Ezra was praying in this way, and while he was imploring and weeping and lying before the temple of God, an exceedingly great assembly of men, women, and children was gathered to him from Israel, and the people wept with much weeping.
verses.10:2: And Shecaniah the son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, answered and said to Ezra, "We have acted unfaithfully against our God and have married foreign wives from the peoples of the land; and now, if there is repentance in Israel concerning this,
verses.10:3: let us make a covenant with the Lord our God to cast out all the wives and those who have been born of them, according to the will of the Lord and of those who fear the command of the Lord our God; let it be done according to the law.
verses.10:4: Arise, it is yours to decide, and we will be with you; be strong, and act."
verses.10:5: So Ezra arose and made the leaders of the priests and of the Levites, and all Israel, swear that they would act according to this word; and they swore.
verses.10:6: And Ezra arose before the house of God and went to the chamber of Jehohanan the son of Eliashib, and entered there; he did not eat bread and did not drink water, for he was mourning the transgression of those who had come from the captivity.
verses.10:7: And a proclamation was sent in Judah and in Jerusalem to all the sons of the exile, that they should be gathered together in Jerusalem;
verses.10:8: and as for everyone who does not come within three days, according to the counsel of the leaders and the elders, all his property will be taken away, and he himself will be cast out from the assembly of the exile.
verses.10:9: Therefore all the men of Judah and Benjamin assembled in Jerusalem within three days; it was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month; and all the people sat in the open square of the house of God, trembling because of the sin and the rains.
verses.10:10: And Ezra the priest arose and said to them, "You have transgressed and have married foreign wives, so as to add to the guilt of Israel.
verses.10:11: And now make confession to the Lord God of your fathers, and do His pleasure, and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign wives."
verses.10:12: And the entire multitude answered and said with a loud voice, "According to your word to us, so let it be done.
verses.10:13: However, because the people are many, and it is the time of rain, and we cannot bear to stand outside, and the work is not of one day or two (for indeed we have sinned greatly in this matter),
verses.10:14: let leaders be appointed in the entire multitude; and let all in our cities who have married foreign wives come at appointed times, and with them the elders, city by city, and the judges of each, until the anger of our God is turned away from us over this sin."
verses.10:15: Therefore Jonathan the son of Asahel and Jahzeiah the son of Tekoa stood over this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them;
verses.10:16: and the sons of the exile did so. And Ezra the priest and the men, the leaders of the families, went into the houses of their fathers, and all of them by their names; and they sat down on the first day of the tenth month to investigate the matter.
verses.10:17: And all the men who had married foreign wives were dealt with by the first day of the first month.
verses.10:18: And among the sons of the priests there were found those who had married foreign wives. Of the sons of Joshua the son of Jozadak, and his brothers: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.
verses.10:19: And they gave their hands that they would put away their wives, and that for their guilt they would offer a ram from the sheep.
verses.10:20: And of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
verses.10:21: And of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
verses.10:22: And of the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
verses.10:23: And of the sons of the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
verses.10:24: And of the singers: Eliashib. And of the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
verses.10:25: And from Israel, of the sons of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eliezer, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
verses.10:26: And of the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
verses.10:27: And of the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
verses.10:28: And of the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, Athlai.
verses.10:29: And of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Ramoth.
verses.10:30: And of the sons of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
verses.10:31: And of the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Joshua, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Simeon,
verses.10:33: And of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, Shimei.
verses.10:34: Of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel,
verses.10:43: Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.
verses.10:44: All these had taken foreign wives, and there were women among them who had borne children.

notes.1:4: The Vulgate shifts from plural ("all the rest... wherever they dwell... what they voluntarily offer") to singular ("assist him... from his place"), reflecting a shift back to the individual returnee of verse 3 or calquing the Hebrew singular. Here and in verses 5 and 7, the Vulgate renders "temple" (templum) where the Hebrew has "house."
notes.1:6: The Vulgate literally reads "assisted their hands" (adjuverunt manus eorum, versus Hebrew "strengthened"), joins both silver and gold as adjectives modifying "vessels" (in vasis argenteis et aureis), and renders the Hebrew term for "costly things" as "furnishings" (supellectili).
notes.1:8: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew Persian-loanword title haggizbar ("the treasurer") as a patronymic proper name, filii Gazabar ("the son of Gazabar"). The Latin forms Mithridatis and Sassabasar are given in their standard English biblical spellings, Mithredath and Sheshbazzar.
notes.1:9: The Vulgate translates the rare Hebrew term mahalapim (variously understood as censers, knives, or duplicates) as cultri ("knives"). It also places "thirty gold goblets" (scyphi aurei triginta) at the end of verse 9 rather than at the beginning of verse 10 as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.1:11: Both the Vulgate and the Hebrew text state a total of five thousand four hundred vessels, although the itemized counts in verses 9-10 sum to two thousand four hundred ninety-nine (possibly because only major categories were listed). The Vulgate also reads active "those who were going up" (his qui ascendebant) from the "exile" (transmigratione, literally removal or deportation) of Babylon.
notes.2:1: The Vulgate reads de captivitate, quam transtulerat ("from the captivity that ... had deported"), using the singular collective noun captivitas for the deported community, whereas the Hebrew has the doubled phrase "from the captivity of the exile whom ... had exiled."
notes.2:2: Here and in 2:6 the Vulgate reads Josue ("Joshua"), matching the fuller form of the name used in Haggai and Zechariah, whereas the Hebrew text of Ezra uses the shortened post-exilic form Yeshua ("Jeshua").
notes.2:6: The Clementine Vulgate punctuates the asyndetic phrase as filiorum Josue: Joab ("of the sons of Joshua: Joab"), without a conjunction; it is commonly understood as referring either to the descendants of both Joshua and Joab or specifically to the Joab branch among Joshua's sons.
notes.2:25: The Vulgate reads Cariathiarim ("Kiriath-jearim", matching Nehemiah 7:29), whereas the Hebrew text of Ezra 2:25 reads the shorter form Kiriath-arim.
notes.2:43: Latin Nathinæi ("Nethinim") transliterates the Hebrew title for the consecrated temple servants.
notes.2:57: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew compound name Pochereth-hazzebaim as a personal name with a clause of origin, Phochereth, qui erant de Asebaim ("Pochereth, who were from Hazzebaim").
notes.2:63: Latin Athersatha transliterates the Persian title ha-Tirshata ("the Tirshatha," meaning "the governor"). Where the Hebrew reads "with Urim and Thummim," the Vulgate renders those terms adjectivally as doctus atque perfectus ("learned and perfect").
notes.2:69: The Vulgate reads impensas operis ("the expenses of the work," where the Hebrew has "treasury of the work") and renders the Hebrew gold coins (darkemonim, "darics") as solidos ("solidi"), the late Roman gold coin.
notes.3:2: The Vulgate renders the high priest's name as Josue ("Joshua"), matching Haggai and Zechariah, whereas the Hebrew text of Ezra uses the shortened post-exilic form "Jeshua."
notes.3:3: The Vulgate specifies altare Dei ("the altar of God") and uses an ablative absolute (deterrentibus eos per circuitum populis terrarum, "while the peoples of the lands all around were terrifying them"), where the Hebrew has "the altar" and "because dread was upon them from the peoples of the lands."
notes.3:10: Latin per manus David ("by the hands of David") preserves the literal idiom meaning according to David's directions; the Vulgate also reads Deum ("God") where the Hebrew has the divine name.
notes.3:12: Following the Clementine Vulgate syntax (templum prius cum fundatum esset, et hoc templum), "when it was founded" modifies the former temple and et ("and") introduces "this temple," whereas the Hebrew connects the laying of the foundation directly to "this house."
notes.4:2: The Vulgate reads ecce nos immolavimus victimas ("look, we have offered sacrifices"), omitting both "to Him" (Hebrew Qere) and "not" (Hebrew Ketiv).
notes.4:3: The Vulgate reads Domino Deo nostro ("to the Lord our God"), where the Hebrew reads "to the Lord, the God of Israel."
notes.4:7: The Vulgate adds accusationis ("of accusation"), renders Aramaic as syriace / sermone syro ("Syriac" / "the Syrian language"), and reads legebatur ("was read") where the Hebrew has "translated."
notes.4:8: Latin Reum Beelteem treats the Aramaic official title be'el-te'em ("commander" or "chancellor") as part of Rehum's proper name (likewise in 4:9, 4:17, and 4:23).
notes.4:10: The Vulgate renders the Aramaic epistolary transition uk'enet ("and now") as in pace ("in peace"), and similarly includes et pacem ("and peace") in 4:17.
notes.5:4: Retaining the first-person plural respondimus ("we answered") of the Aramaic, the Vulgate presents this verse as the Jews' reply giving the builders' names, whereas the Septuagint has the third person ("they said").
notes.5:5: Latin satisfacerent adversus accusationem illam ("give satisfaction against that accusation") is a Vulgate-distinct rendering where the Aramaic speaks of sending back a letter regarding the matter.
notes.5:8: The Vulgate renders Aramaic 'eben gelal ("huge/heavy stones") as lapide impolito ("unpolished stone").
notes.5:17: The Vulgate renders Aramaic beit ginzayya ("house of treasures" or "treasury") as bibliotheca regis ("the library of the king").
notes.6:4: The Vulgate reads "unpolished stones" (lapidibus impolitis) and plural "likewise courses of new timber" (et sic ordines de lignis novis), whereas the Aramaic Masoretic Text refers to large stones and a single course of new timber.
notes.6:5: The closing clause "which were also placed in the temple of God" (quæ et posita sunt in templo Dei) is a Vulgate perfect passive indicative statement, whereas the Aramaic expresses a command to deposit them in the house of God.
notes.6:9: The Vulgate lists "young goats" (hædos) where the Aramaic lists rams, and translates "according to the word of the priests" as "according to the rite of the priests" (secundum ritum sacerdotum).
notes.6:11: The Vulgate translates the penalty on the offender's house with the Roman legal term publicetur ("be confiscated" to the public treasury), whereas the Aramaic specifies that it be turned into a refuse heap.
notes.6:19: The Clementine Vulgate reads "the sons of Israel of the exile" (filii Israël transmigrationis), including "Israel" where the Hebrew reads simply "the sons of the exile."
notes.7:5: The Vulgate renders Aaron's title as "the priest from the beginning" (sacerdotis ab initio), taking the Hebrew word for "chief" (rosh) in its temporal sense of "beginning."
notes.7:6: The Vulgate construes "Israel" as the indirect object ("which the Lord God gave to Israel"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "which the Lord, the God of Israel, gave."
notes.7:12: The Vulgate renders the Aramaic honorific and epistolary transition ("and now") into classical Latin letter form as "most learned ... greetings" (doctissimo, salutem).
notes.7:21: In the Clementine Vulgate punctuation, "and from me" (et a me.) concludes the list of funding sources begun in verse 20, whereas the Aramaic joins it to the opening of King Artaxerxes's decree.
notes.8:3: The Vulgate places "Of the sons of Shecaniah" at the start of verse 3 in apposition to "the sons of Parosh," whereas the Hebrew attaches "of the sons of Shecaniah" to Hattush in verse 2.
notes.8:5: The Vulgate reads "Ezekiel" (Ezechiel) where the Hebrew text reads "Jahaziel," and like the Hebrew omits an individual name before "the son of Ezekiel."
notes.8:22: The Vulgate reads "help" (auxilium) rather than "a force of soldiers," connects "in goodness" (in bonitate) to those who seek God rather than to God's hand ("for good"), and lists three attributes ("His dominion, and His strength, and wrath") where the Hebrew has two.
notes.8:26: The Vulgate reads "one hundred silver vessels" (vasa argentea centum), without the weight unit "talents" that accompanies the silver vessels in the Hebrew text.
notes.8:27: The Vulgate translates the Persian darics of the Hebrew as Roman gold solidi (solidos) and uses the distributive numeral millenos ("a thousand each").
notes.9:8: Taking the underlying Hebrew noun in its sense of "supplication" rather than "favor," the Vulgate reads "our supplication has been made before the Lord our God" (facta est deprecatio nostra apud Dominum Deum nostrum), whereas the Hebrew speaks of grace shown by God.
notes.9:11: "From mouth to mouth" (ab ore usque ad os) is the Vulgate's literal rendering of the Hebrew idiom meaning "from end to end"; the Vulgate also adds "and of the other lands" (ceterarumque terrarum).
notes.9:13: The Vulgate reads "have delivered us from our iniquity" (liberasti nos de iniquitate nostra), whereas the Hebrew reads "have punished us less than our iniquities deserve."
notes.9:14: Unlike the Hebrew, which begins verse 14 as a question, the Vulgate continues verse 13 with a negative purpose clause ("so that we would not turn back...") and omits the negative in the following question ("Are You angry...?" versus Hebrew "Would You not be angry...?").
notes.10:2: The Vulgate reads "if there is repentance" (si est pœnitentia), forming a conditional clause with verse 3, whereas the Hebrew text reads "there is hope."
notes.10:9: Both here (pro peccato, "because of the sin") and in 10:14 (super peccato hoc, "over this sin"), the Vulgate specifies "sin" where the Hebrew text reads "matter."
notes.10:15: The Vulgate reads "Therefore ... stood over this" (Igitur ... steterunt super hoc), portraying these men as presiding over the measure rather than opposing it, and has Thecue ("Tekoa," matching the Septuagint) where the Hebrew reads "Tikvah."
notes.10:16: The Vulgate reads "went into the houses of their fathers" (abierunt ... in domos patrum suorum), whereas the Hebrew text states that Ezra selected men according to their fathers' houses.
notes.10:25: The Vulgate reads "Eliezer" (matching the Septuagint), whereas the Hebrew text reads "Eleazar."
notes.10:31: The Vulgate reads Josue ("Joshua," as in 10:18), whereas the Hebrew text reads "Isshijah."
notes.10:44: The Vulgate renders the difficult Hebrew ending cleanly as "there were women among them who had borne children" (fuerunt ex eis mulieres, quæ pepererant filios).
